newsitem.title: ERITREA: Sudan rebels insist they seized district.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels insist they seized district.

text.p: Sudanese rebels reiterated on Wednesday they had seized a district in northeast Sudan, dismissing a government denial as an "absolute lie".
Sudanese Culture and Information Minister Brigadier Al-Tayeb Ibrahim Mohamed Khair said on Tuesday Aqiq district on Sudan's Red Sea coast was still in the hands of government forces.
"This is an absolute lie," said Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) spokesman Yassir Arman in Eritrea's capital Asmara.
He said Aqiq was occupied by forces of the rebel National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and government forces had withdrawn from the garrisons of Adart and Adib and they had been occupied by rebels.
He said government forces had withdrawn towards Tokar, the third biggest town in Red Sea state, and rebels were advancing.
Khair told a news conference in Khartoum the army contained a joint Eritrean and rebel offensive in Karora district near Sudan's border with Eritrea after destroying two tanks.
"The enemy is now under seige for six days and in very low morale in Wadi Ganit and outlaw claims that they have captured Aqiq is a lie and part of psychological warfare," Khair said.
SPLA leader John Garang said on Tuesday the rebel coalition had seized Aqiq, Karora, Itairba and Agiti districts in the northeast last week and over the weekend in a new offensive.

Tokar is 150 km (90 miles) southeast of Port Sudan, the country's main link to the outside world. Eritrea and Ethiopia have denied accusations from Khartoum that their troops are fighting alongside the rebels in the northeast and east.

The SPLA has been fighting since 1983 for greater autonomy or independence for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arabised north. It and its allies say they want a popular uprising in Khartoum to topple the Islamist government.
Arman said on Wednesday the SPLA had captured 400 Ugandan rebels of the West Nile Bank Front (WNBF) along with government troops when it overran the southern town of Yei on March 12.

"We captured in Yei 400 prisoners of war from the West Nile Bank Front. They are Ugandans fighting with NIF (National Islamic Front) forces around Yei," said Arman, adding they included deputy WNBF chairman Brigadier-General Abdul el-Ateef.
He said the prisoners proved Khartoum was "harbouring terrorism" because WNBF rebels were based in southern Sudan. Khartoum accuses Uganda of backing the SPLA and supplying it with arms.
